title: Nobody wrote that it hit him.
description:
Nobody wrote that it hit him. In the passages read, Newton's story is of an apple falling while he sat thinking, not of a blow to the head.

It comes from his friend William Stukeley. Stukeley's account describes tea in the garden under apple trees, and Newton saying the idea was occasioned by the fall of an apple, as he sat in contemplative mood.

When, according to the Associated Press, Newton shared the story with Stukeley over tea.

Newton never wrote it down. Physics World says he appears to have repeated the story often in later life, but never wrote it down.

The year the account was first published, long after the 1660s plague retreat it describes.

Put the handwritten manuscript online, with the apple story on pages 42 and 43.

The apple stays. The bump on the head goes.

Sources:
- https://www.scientificamerican.com/blog/observations/whats-the-real-story-with-newton-and-the-apple-see-for-yourself/: read. Established that the account is by William Stukeley, a contemporary, not published until 1752; the quoted words It was occasion'd by the fall of an apple, as he sat in contemplative mood; the garden and tea under apple trees; and that the legend appears in other accounts of the time.
- https://phys.org/news183018659.html: read (AP wire story). Established a spring afternoon in 1726 over tea, that the manuscript was posted online by the Royal Society on Monday 18 January 2010, and the plague retreat in the mid 1660s.
- https://physicsworld.com/a/newtons-apple-the-birth-of-a/: read (18 January 2010). Established that Stukeley was a friend, that Newton appears to have repeated the story often in later life but never wrote it down, and that the apple story is on pages 42 and 43 of the manuscript on the Royal Society site.
